Commit everything when you are done.
`matchEach` must be a named export from the package entry point.
`matchEach` is a top-level function callable with a value argument: `matchEach(value)`.
`matchEach` evaluates ALL registered patterns against the input — every `.with()` clause whose pattern matches contributes its handler's result, not just the first match.
contracts.adverse_condition: Input matches more than one registered pattern; a short-circuit implementation would only collect the first.

contracts.text: Results are collected into an array returned in the order clauses were declared.
contracts.adverse_condition: Patterns are declared in a different order than they would naturally match, and at least two results are not identical, so swapping would be detectable.

contracts.text: `matchEach` exposes the same builder API as `match`, including all `.with()` overloads: single-pattern, multi-pattern, and guard variants.
`matchEach` exposes a `.when()` method.
`matchEach` exposes a `.returnType()` method.
`matchEach` exposes a `.narrow()` method.
Every `.with()` call must accept patterns against the original input type, not the progressively narrowed remainder — because all branches are always evaluated.
contracts.adverse_condition: Input is a discriminated union and `.narrow()` was called previously; a narrowing-based API would reject a pattern already excluded.

contracts.text: Exhaustiveness tracking narrows the internal type so `.exhaustive()` can verify all cases are handled.
`.narrow()` updates both the internal tracking type and the input type for subsequent `.with()` calls to exclude handled cases.
`.run()` returns an array of all matching handler results.
contracts.adverse_condition: Only one pattern matches; a single-value return would be indistinguishable from an array of length 1.

contracts.text: `.exhaustive()` returns an array of all matching handler results.
contracts.adverse_condition: Only one pattern matches; a single-value return would be indistinguishable from an array of length 1.

contracts.text: If nothing matched, `.run()` throws `NonExhaustiveError`.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one pattern matches; the throw path is not triggered.

contracts.text: If nothing matched, `.exhaustive()` throws `NonExhaustiveError`.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one pattern matches; the throw path is not triggered.

contracts.text: `.exhaustive()` enforces compile-time exhaustiveness: it should be a type error if not all input cases are handled.

`.exhaustive()` accepts an optional fallback handler function; when provided and no pattern matches at runtime, the fallback is called and its result is returned in a single-element array instead of throwing.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one pattern matches; the fallback must not be invoked and the result must not be a single-element fallback array.

contracts.text: `.otherwise(handler)` returns `[handler(value)]` when no patterns matched.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one pattern matches; this branch must not be taken.

contracts.text: `.otherwise(handler)` returns the array of all matching results when at least one pattern matched; the default handler is not included in that array.
contracts.adverse_condition: No patterns match; the other branch is taken instead.

contracts.text: `.otherwise()` never throws.
contracts.adverse_condition: Input fails to match any pattern; a throwing implementation would be detected.

contracts.text: `.tap(callback)` registers a side-effect callback and returns a new `matchEach` for continued chaining.
When the expression is evaluated, each tap point calls its callback once per result that has been collected up to that point in declaration order.
contracts.adverse_condition: Multiple tap points exist and the number of results accumulated differs between them; counting callbacks per tap verifies per-point semantics.

contracts.text: Tap does not affect the results array.
contracts.adverse_condition: A tap callback mutates its argument or returns a value that could be confused with a result.

contracts.text: Multiple tap points can be stacked.
contracts.adverse_condition: Only one tap point is used; stacking cannot be verified.

contracts.text: Tap callbacks execute inside compiled functions produced by `.toFunction()`.
Tap callbacks execute inside compiled functions produced by `.toExhaustiveFunction()`.
Tap callbacks execute inside compiled functions produced by `.toPartialFunction()`.
`matchEach` can be called without a value argument using explicit type parameters to build a reusable compiled matcher.
contracts.adverse_condition: The zero-argument form must be distinguishable from the value-bearing form at the type level.

contracts.text: `.toFunction()` compiles the registered clauses into a reusable `(input) => output[]` function.
`.toFunction()` throws `NonExhaustiveError` if no pattern matches at runtime.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one pattern matches; the throw path is not triggered.

contracts.text: `.toExhaustiveFunction()` enforces compile-time exhaustiveness: it should be a type error if not all input cases are handled.
`.toPartialFunction()` compiles into a function that returns `output[] | undefined`.
`.toPartialFunction()` returns `undefined` when no patterns match instead of throwing.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one pattern matches; the undefined return path is not triggered.

contracts.text: `.toPartialFunction()` never throws.
contracts.adverse_condition: Input fails to match any pattern; a throwing implementation would be detected.

contracts.text: Selections via `P.select()` must produce independent results across multiple calls of any compiled function.
contracts.adverse_condition: The same compiled function is called twice with different inputs; shared mutable selection state would leak values across invocations.

contracts.text: Each clause maintains independent selection state. Named selections from one clause must not leak into another clause's handler.
contracts.adverse_condition: Two clauses use the same named selection via `P.select('name')`; cross-clause leakage would produce the wrong value in at least one handler.

contracts.text: `.exhaustive()` with a fallback handler: when patterns do match, the fallback is not called and the result array contains only the matching handler results (not the fallback result).
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one pattern matches; invoking the fallback or including its result would be detectable.

contracts.text: `.exhaustive()` with a fallback handler: when no pattern matches, the fallback is called exactly once and its return value is wrapped in a single-element array.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one pattern matches; this path should not execute.

contracts.text: The `.with()` multi-pattern overload submits each of the N patterns against the same original input, and the handler result is included once per `.with()` clause (not once per sub-pattern) when at least one sub-pattern matches.
contracts.adverse_condition: A clause supplies multiple patterns and more than one sub-pattern matches the input; result duplication would signal per-sub-pattern rather than per-clause semantics.

contracts.text: A guard-function `.with(pattern, guard).handler(...)` only contributes its result when both the pattern matches and the guard returns true.
contracts.adverse_condition: Input matches the pattern but the guard returns false; the handler must be skipped.

contracts.text: The ordering of results in the output array of `.run()` matches the textual declaration order of the `.with()` clauses, even when a later clause's pattern is more general than an earlier one.
contracts.adverse_condition: Two clauses both match, the later clause is more general, and results are distinguishable; swapping would be detected.

contracts.text: `.toFunction()` with explicit type parameters (no-argument `matchEach` call) produces a function whose parameter type matches the explicit type argument.
contracts.adverse_condition: The explicit type parameter differs from the type that would be inferred from a value argument.

contracts.text: `.toExhaustiveFunction()` throws `NonExhaustiveError` at runtime if no pattern matches.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one pattern matches; throw path not triggered.
